spec_gaps.description: feat-prove-daemon-lifecycle's own behavior sentence includes a third clause -- 'killing the daemon mid-session leaves the next call succeeding with no client-side re-initialization' -- which is INV-SHIM-3's exact text ('a daemon restart is invisible to the client ... subsequent calls succeed with no client-side re-initialisation'). Not designed here: this feature's falsifier cites only INV-SHIM-1, INV-SHIM-2 and INV-SHIM-4 -- never INV-SHIM-3 -- and INV-SHIM-3 is already cited by feat-mcp-shim's own falsifier ('a daemon restart mid-session requires the client to re-initialize instead of the shim reconnecting transparently [INV-SHIM-3]'), a different (build) feature. Treating the behavior sentence's third clause as this plan's scope would duplicate a condition that belongs to feat-mcp-shim's own test plan; this plan covers only the three invariants this feature's falsifier actually names.

Neither INV-SHIM-1/2/4's text nor feat-prove-daemon-lifecycle's context note states a numeric bound for how long convergence-to-one-daemon (INV-SHIM-2) or full shutdown-and-reap of every JDT LS child (INV-SHIM-4) is allowed to take before the assertion is made -- unlike the per-call deadline covered by docs/cross-cutting.md#X-001 (which is a different, open, cross-cutting concern about tool-call response time, not daemon start-up/shutdown time). Not treated as a blocking ambiguity: the conditions below describe the outcome to poll for (eventually exactly one daemon pid; eventually no live JDT LS child in the process table) and leave the concrete poll/settle timeout as the eventual test implementation's fixture choice, since no spec value exists to trace a specific number to.
